findings.title: $__range queries no longer routed to non-splitting path because detection happens after interpolation
findings.body: In `runSplitQuery`, `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` is now invoked on every kept target (line 299) BEFORE `partition(..., query => !querySupportsSplitting(query))` is evaluated (line 300). `querySupportsSplitting` relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` which uses `expr.includes('$__range')`. Because `templateSrv.replace` substitutes `$__range`/`$__range_s`/`$__range_ms` with numeric values, those strings are gone from `expr` by the time the check runs. As a result, queries such as `rate({app="frontend"}[$__range])` are now placed in `normalQueries` and get split across chunks instead of being routed to `nonSplittingQueries`. This is exactly the case the in-source comment on lines 285-287 warns against: when the chunk reaches the backend, `$__range` would be (re-)interpolated against the split timeRange and the result would be incorrect. Before this PR, `runSplitQuery` did not interpolate, so the `isQueryWithRangeVariable` check worked. The interpolation must be deferred until after the `$__range` / `querySupportsSplitting` classification, or the non-splitting partition must be computed from the original `request.targets`.

findings.title: Mock `replace` does not handle built-in variables, masking the $__range regression
findings.body: The new test `'Interpolates queries before execution'` (and the corresponding one in `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts`) override `replace` to substitute only `$__auto` and `$step`. They leave `$__range`/`$__range_s`/`$__range_ms` untouched. The real Grafana `templateSrv.replace` substitutes these built-ins. Because the mock preserves them, any future test using `$__range` will pass (the substring check finds the literal) while production silently drops them, so the regression described for `querySplitting.ts` cannot be caught by the current mock setup. The mocks should also replace built-in variables (e.g. `$__range` → `300s`) to reflect production, and a test asserting that a `$__range` query is not split should be added.

findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice on the shard-splitting path
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` (lines 49-52) maps every kept target through `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` and hands the resulting array to `splitQueriesByStreamShard`, which then constructs a `subRequest` whose `targets` are derived from those already-interpolated queries and passes that subRequest to `runSplitQuery` (line 163). `runSplitQuery` now also calls `applyTemplateVariables` on every kept target. So in the shard path each target is interpolated twice. Beyond wasted work, this is fragile: if `templateSrv.replace` (or a downstream format handler) is ever non-idempotent for any variable, the second pass would produce different output. The interpolation in `runShardSplitQuery` is redundant once `runSplitQuery` performs it itself; one of the two should be removed.
